headline: Learned models predict protein stability and binding from embeddings and structure
label: Learned Models Of Protein Stability
summary: Recent preprints test how much structure adds beyond protein language model embeddings for stability and binding predictions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations, most often protein language model embeddings, applied to predicting stability and binding energetics. An ablation on mutation-induced ΔTm prediction reports that PLM embeddings dominate, with structure adding value mainly for atypical cases, while ProtBFF injects biophysical priors into residue-level representations to improve protein-protein ΔΔG prediction. Sparse autoencoders applied to fine-tuned ESM-2 nanobody thermostability embeddings yield interpretable features linked to stabilizing and destabilizing effects, shifting emphasis from prediction toward mechanism. LLPSense extends the embedding-based approach by adding temperature, concentration and solvent parameters for condition-dependent phase separation. BindMecNet adds atom-residue interaction maps for affinity prediction. Generative items, including SeedProteo, SeedFold, DREAM and PocketX, are adjacent rather than central. What is new is interpretability of fine-tuned embeddings alongside explicit conditional inputs.
